title: Preparing a Victorian sale
description: What to have ready before marketing a Victorian property: the section 32 vendor statement and the documents that feed it, plus agent and buyer-facing obligations. Summarised from Consumer Affairs Victoria, the Building and Plumbing Commission and the State Revenue Office.

sources.title: Contracts and disclosure statements – estate agents
Underquoting information for real estate agents

items.title: Engage a conveyancer or lawyer to prepare the section 32 statement and contract
Section 32 vendor statement ready before any buyer signs
items.detail: Covers mortgages, easements, planning controls, rates and taxes, building permits and insurance.

items.title: Owner-builder defects report and domestic building insurance if selling within 6.5 years
Pool registered with council and barrier certificate lodged
SRO property clearance certificate ordered by your conveyancer
Copies of the Victorian due diligence checklist for open inspections and a link in your listing
Read the sales authority and agree the estimated selling price with your agent
Confirm the reserve price in writing at least 7 days before an auction
Notice of intention to sell given to any renter at least 14 days before showing
